games.title: Return To Castle Hu-Nam
games.public_description: Fire plasma through an office invasion; early Wolfenstein parody title

ai_authorship.quote: Just like many of my games on here so far I like to stack feature-heavy with many many AI interactions on Claude. (I start with a game-oriented AI like Rosebud or CoPlay or Jabali) and then take my end product into general Claude or some other general AI -after- it’s mostly stable as a game where going incrementally is safer.

guest_gameplay.response: The Open Office level opened with HUD controls and 13 targets. Space fired the weapon and changed the displayed PLASMA count from 99 to 98.

games.title: Quantum Foam Dive
games.public_description: Start a passive science dive and watch depth and score rise

ai_authorship.quote: There wasn’t enough AI credit budget left on the week (Claude Opus was down to 4% left until Tuesday at 9am) so the process was like this: make a big huge text file out of chatting in the X/Twitter sidebar with Grok initially in Javascript text. Then I took it to Ziva AI within Godot and said translate these JS scripts entirely into Godot. And it converted to GDScript, there wasn’t any C# code generated this time around. Then when Ziva was as close as I could safely get (it had only $20 credit) I turned to Claude’s 4% left and said “ok Opus can you check this for bad errors that Ziva was well-meaning but had strewn all over the place” and Claude was my hero and said aye aye sir.
ai_authorship.source_type: official itch.io game description; game-specific AI Disclosure lists AI Assisted, Code, Graphics, Sounds, Text

guest_gameplay.input: Pressed Escape to reach the title menu, then Space (the displayed Start Dive control).
guest_gameplay.response: The player entered the dive scene; the HUD showed Score 17, Depth 120 m, Layer 1, “Concepts 0 – Shield ready,” and the diver sprite.
guest_gameplay.access: Guest direct creator-linked Godot HTML5 player; no account or sign-in.

warnings: Creator describes the current game as a passive educational idler: no danger to the diver and the score rises over time. The test confirmed starting a dive; deeper interaction was not assessed.
